title: Pennywhistle: Initiative tracker for token-cost reductions (batching / KV caching / quantization)
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
The Pennywhistle initiative is a coordinated program to reduce host API token cost by ~20% for mid-tail production workloads through three levers: micro-batching heuristics, adaptive KV prefix caching with controlled TTLs, and conservative quantization rollout (model-family + per-workload profile). This ticket centralizes planning, experiments, rollout gating, and OKR tracking for the initiative across PM, Eng, and DevEx.

Goals:
- Primary: Reduce cost per 1M generated tokens for our hosted API by 15–25% on targeted workloads without >1% increase in customer-reported quality regressions.
- Latency guardrail: Maintain p95 generation latency within current SLA (target: no regression >10% from baseline).
- Observability: Provide token-level and route-level dashboards to measure impact and detect regressions automatically.

Scope & approach:
1) Micro-batching runtime experiments (continuous batching + tail-aware batching policy). Field trials will compare baseline batching to new heuristics across small/medium/large sequence lengths.
2) KV caching: implement adaptive TTLs per-customer and hot-prefix detection to increase hit rate while bounding stale-response risk.
3) Quantization: phased quant profiles (float16 -> q4_0 -> q4_1) validated by per-prompt quality evals and automated regression checks.

Deliverables:
- Experiment matrix and instrumentation (A/A baselines, A/B lanes, canary lanes).
- Dashboard + alerts (cost, hit-rate, p95/p99 latency, qualitative eval pass-rate).
- Rollout playbook with gate checks and rollback criteria.
- Post-mortem template and runbook for detected regressions.

Alignment to OKRs:
- OKR: Reduce hosted inference unit cost by 18% YTD. Pennywhistle is a primary contributor for Q2 experiments.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Maya Patel (owner)
- Eng leads: Luca Moreno (runtime), Priya Singh (observability)
- Design/DevEx: Ryan O’Hara (docs & onboarding)
- Data/Research: Elena Rodriguez (quality evals)

Why distinct from other efforts:
We will treat Pennywhistle as a tightly scoped, hypothesis driven program with an explicit experiment-to-rollout pipeline and operator-facing guardrails. The initiative emphasizes per-workload profiling + conservative rollouts rather than broad, global defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented experiment lanes capturing cost per 1M tokens, aggregate token throughput, and p95/p99 latency for target routes
KV cache adaptive TTL implemented behind feature flag with measured hit-rate uplift >= 12% on target workloads
Micro-batching policy implemented in runtime with no more than 10% p95 latency regression on canary traffic
Quant profile validated on representative prompt set with automated BLEU/ROUGE-style and task-specific metrics showing <1% quality regression for target customers
Dashboards and alerts live in Console with runbook links and owner assignments
Rollout playbook documented with clear gate thresholds and rollback steps
kpis: quality_regressions_detected: percent of prompts failing eval gates (target <1%)
deployment_rollouts_successful: percent of canaries promoted without rollback
